description: Self-authored synthetic fixture: 4 fictional personas x 4 conversation sessions (16 sessions), 40 questions. NOT LoCoMo; see docs/SI-130-memory-benchmark.md.

sessions.text:
Priya: Hi! I'm Priya Nair. I live in Austin, Texas, and I work as a pediatric nurse at the children's hospital downtown.
Assistant: Welcome, Priya. How long have you been nursing?
Priya: Six years now. I love working with kids, even on the hard days.
Assistant: Do you have any pets at home?
Priya: Yes — I have a golden retriever named Biscuit. He's three years old and sheds absolutely everywhere.
Assistant: Anyone else in the household?
Priya: Just me and Biscuit. My sister Ananya lives across town, and she's getting married in June, so I'm helping her plan the wedding.
Assistant: That sounds like a busy spring for you.
Priya: It is, but a good kind of busy.

Priya: Training update: I signed up for a half marathon in October, so I'm running four mornings a week now.
Assistant: That's a big goal, Priya. How is the training going?
Priya: Slowly but surely. I also joined a climbing gym — I've been doing rock climbing twice a week, which helps my legs more than I expected.
Assistant: Any dietary restrictions your training plan should know about?
Priya: Yes, important one: I'm allergic to peanuts. Even a small amount of peanuts sends me to urgent care, so I read every label.
Assistant: Noted. How do you get to your training sessions?
Priya: I drive my blue Honda Civic. It's old and the air conditioning is temperamental, but it gets me there.
Assistant: Sounds like a full schedule.
Priya: It keeps me out of trouble, mostly.

Priya: Big news — I moved! I left Texas last month and I'm now living in Denver, Colorado.
Assistant: Congratulations, Priya! How are you settling into the new city?
Priya: Denver is a beautiful city. Biscuit adores the snow, which I did not expect from a Texas dog.
Assistant: Have you picked up anything new there?
Priya: I started taking a pottery class on Thursday evenings. Last week I made a very lopsided bowl and I'm weirdly proud of it.
Assistant: Any other plans in the new city?
Priya: Mostly exploring neighborhoods and finding a good running route before winter really arrives.
Priya: I also started volunteering at an animal shelter on Sundays, walking the dogs who are waiting for adoption.
Assistant: Sounds like the move agrees with you.
Priya: It really does.

Priya: Car update: I finally traded in my old car and bought a silver Subaru Outback. The all-wheel drive will help with Colorado winters.
Assistant: A sensible upgrade, Priya. Any travel plans with it?
Priya: Actually yes — I'm planning a trip to Kyoto in the spring. I've been saving for two years and I want to see the cherry blossoms.
Assistant: Wonderful. How is the pottery going?
Priya: I made a whole set of mugs in my Thursday class. Glazing is harder than it looks.
Assistant: And Biscuit?
Priya: Biscuit has claimed the passenger seat of the Outback as his personal throne.
Assistant: As is his right.
Priya: Exactly.

Marcus: Hey, I'm Marcus Bell. I live in Chicago and I work as a firefighter with Engine Company 18.
Assistant: Welcome, Marcus. How long have you been with the department?
Marcus: Eleven years. Before that I was in the Army for four.
Assistant: Do you have a dog? You mentioned one before.
Marcus: I do — a black Labrador named Pepper. She rides along to the station on my days off and the whole crew spoils her.
Assistant: Any hobbies outside work?
Marcus: I play an acoustic guitar most evenings. Nothing fancy, mostly old blues songs. My phone plan is with Verizon, which matters because the station gets terrible reception on some carriers.
Assistant: A firefighter, a guitarist, and a dog person.
Marcus: That about sums me up.

Marcus: I've started learning French this month. There's a trip next year I want to be ready for, and I refuse to be the tourist pointing at menus.
Assistant: Bon courage, Marcus! How are the lessons going?
Marcus: Slow. The pronunciation is humbling. In other news, I coach a Little League baseball team on weekends — twelve very energetic nine-year-olds.
Assistant: That is a lot of energy. Do you have any downtime rituals?
Marcus: I bake sourdough bread every Sunday morning. My starter is named Clint Eastwood, for no reason I can defend.
Assistant: And the gym?
Marcus: I joined a CrossFit gym near the station. The 6 a.m. workouts are brutal but they keep me honest.
Assistant: French, baseball, bread, and burpees.
Marcus: My calendar is a cry for help, honestly.

Marcus: Quick phone update: I switched my phone plan to T-Mobile last week. The reception at the station is finally decent.
Assistant: Glad to hear it, Marcus. What else is new?
Marcus: I bought an old motorcycle — a 1968 Triumph I'm restoring in my garage. Right now it's mostly a pile of parts and optimism.
Assistant: A restoration project! How is Pepper taking the garage time?
Marcus: She supervises from a dog bed in the corner and judges my mechanical skills.
Assistant: Any progress on the French?
Marcus: I can now order coffee and apologize for my French, in French. Progress.
Assistant: That's the most important sentence in any language.
Marcus: Agreed.

Marcus: Gym change: I left my old gym and joined a boxing gym downtown. Turns out I like hitting a heavy bag more than doing burpees.
Assistant: A new chapter, Marcus. Any big plans coming up?
Marcus: Yes! I finally booked the trip — I'm going to Paris in the fall. Two weeks, and I've already mapped out every bakery I want to visit.
Assistant: Your sourdough research continues abroad.
Marcus: Exactly. Pepper will stay with my neighbor, who she loves more than me, so no guilt there.
Assistant: And the Triumph?
Marcus: It runs! Roughly. It starts, which I'm counting as a victory.
Assistant: Paris, boxing, and a running Triumph.
Marcus: A good year.

Tomoko: Hello, I'm Tomoko Abe. I live in San Francisco, and I grew up in Nara, in Japan.
Assistant: Welcome, Tomoko. What do you do for work?
Tomoko: I'm a graphic designer at Northwind Studio, a small studio near the waterfront. We mostly do branding for restaurants.
Assistant: Do you have any pets?
Tomoko: I have a tabby cat named Miso. She is fourteen pounds of pure confidence and she sits on my keyboard during video calls.
Assistant: How do you spend your Sundays?
Tomoko: I volunteer at a food bank on Sundays, packing boxes for the morning distribution. It has become the anchor of my week.
Assistant: That is a lovely routine.
Tomoko: It keeps me grounded.

Tomoko: I took my film photography camera out this weekend — I shoot film photography, mostly street scenes around the Mission.
Assistant: Wonderful, Tomoko. Do you develop the film yourself?
Tomoko: Not yet, but I want to learn. My brother Kenji lives in Osaka, and he keeps sending me photos he took there so we can compare cities.
Assistant: A sibling photography exchange. What else fills your weekends?
Tomoko: I grow shiso and tomatoes on my balcony. The shiso is thriving; the tomatoes are an ongoing negotiation.
Assistant: Any other projects?
Tomoko: I'm scanning my grandfather's old negatives. Some of them are from the 1960s and they're beautiful.
Assistant: That sounds like a treasure.
Tomoko: It really is.

Tomoko: Work news: I left my old studio and started a new job at Harbor Press, a publishing company. I'm an art director there now, designing book covers.
Assistant: Congratulations, Tomoko! How is the new role?
Tomoko: Busy and wonderful. Designing covers means I read manuscripts on my commute, which I love.
Assistant: Any new activities this season?
Tomoko: I joined a community choir that rehearses on Tuesday nights. I'm an alto, and our director is very patient with us.
Assistant: And Miso?
Tomoko: Miso has strong opinions about my singing practice. She leaves the room.
Assistant: Critics everywhere.
Tomoko: The harshest one weighs fourteen pounds.

Tomoko: I moved across the bay last month — I now live in Berkeley, in a one-bedroom apartment with much better light for my plants.
Assistant: A big change, Tomoko. How is the new neighborhood?
Tomoko: Quiet and leafy. The commute to the office is longer, but the morning train ride is good reading time.
Assistant: Are you teaching anything these days?
Tomoko: Yes — I teach a photography workshop on Saturdays at the community arts center. Beginners, mostly, and I love their questions.
Assistant: And the choir?
Tomoko: Still singing on Tuesdays. We have a concert in December.
Assistant: Berkeley suits you.
Tomoko: I think it does.

Diego: Hi, I'm Diego Fuentes. I live in Miami, and I'm a high school math teacher — algebra and geometry, mostly.
Assistant: Welcome, Diego. How long have you been teaching?
Diego: Eight years. My grandmother lives in Havana, and she's the one who taught me to love numbers when I was a kid.
Assistant: Do you have any pets?
Diego: I have an orange cat named Oliver. He is enormous, unbothered, and convinced that my laptop is a heating pad.
Assistant: How do you get around the city?
Diego: I drive a red Mazda hatchback. And on Saturdays I play soccer with a recreational league at the park — I've been on the same team for five years.
Assistant: Teacher, cat owner, soccer player.
Diego: That's the whole resume.

Diego: I've been learning Portuguese for a few months now. There's a trip next year I'm preparing for, and I want to actually talk to people when I get there.
Assistant: Boa sorte, Diego! How are the lessons?
Diego: The vocabulary is fine; the nasal vowels are defeating me. At school, I also run a chess club on Wednesday afternoons — my students are ruthlessly good.
Assistant: Any music in your life?
Diego: I play bass guitar in a small jazz band with two friends from college. We rehearse on Fridays and play maybe three gigs a year.
Assistant: And Oliver?
Diego: Oliver attends every rehearsal and sleeps through all of them.
Assistant: The calmest audience in Miami.
Diego: By far.

Diego: Car news: I sold my old hatchback and bought a green Jeep Wrangler. I have wanted one since I was sixteen.
Assistant: Congratulations, Diego! Any plans for it?
Diego: Beach drives, mostly. At school I've started mentoring a robotics team — we meet after class twice a week and we're building a robot for the regional competition.
Assistant: From algebra to robots.
Diego: The students keep me on my toes. The robot, less so — it currently only drives in circles.
Assistant: How is the Portuguese coming?
Diego: I can hold a five-minute conversation now, as long as nobody talks back too fast.
Assistant: Progress is progress.
Diego: That's my motto this year.

Diego: I hung up my cleats this season and I've taken up surfing instead. Saturday mornings at the beach, falling off a board repeatedly.
Assistant: A new sport, Diego! How is it going?
Diego: Humbling, but the ocean is a good teacher. Bigger news: I booked the trip — I'm flying to Lisbon in July for two weeks.
Assistant: Your Portuguese will get a real workout.
Diego: That's the plan. The jazz band is on pause while our drummer travels, so my Fridays are free for once.
Assistant: And Oliver?
Diego: Oliver will stay with my sister, who spoils him even more than I do.
Assistant: Surfing, Lisbon, and a spoiled cat.
Diego: A good summer ahead.
